name: Voiden MCP Client
description: Connect to an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server over HTTP — remote or local — and run a single operation against it — list/call tools, list/read resources, list/get prompts — the same way .void files already test REST and GraphQL requests.
author: Voiden Team
readme: MCP client extension. Insert an /mcp-client block, point it at a Streamable-HTTP MCP server (remote or local, e.g. http://localhost:3000/mcp), pick an operation (list_tools, call_tool, list_resources, read_resource, list_prompts, get_prompt), and run it like any other request. Phase 1: HTTP transport only — no stdio/local-process servers yet.

blocks.description: Owns 3 block types for MCP server connection, operation, and response rendering

requestPipeline.description: Registers handlers for building MCP requests and rendering MCP responses (HTTP transport)

patterns.name: MCP Server Config
patterns.description: Detects a pasted {"mcpServers": {...}} or {"servers": {...}} JSON config (Claude Desktop / Cursor / VS Code / Windsurf style) — every HTTP-transport entry becomes a block, not just the first; the first updates an existing mcp-connection block in place, each additional one is appended as its own new block

features: Connect to any Streamable-HTTP MCP server, remote or running on localhost
list_tools / call_tool / list_resources / read_resource / list_prompts / get_prompt operations
Paste a Claude Desktop / Cursor / VS Code / Windsurf style mcpServers or VS Code servers JSON config to fill in URL + headers — every server in the config becomes its own block, not just the first
mcp-remote bridge entries (npx -y mcp-remote <url>) unwrap into the real remote URL and headers automatically, no local process spawned
MCP responses render through the same shared code viewer every other block uses — JSON syntax highlighting, search, and selection, with JSON-encoded text content auto-detected and pretty-printed
Reuses existing Auth block for HTTP-transport authentication
Reuses existing assertions-table against MCP responses
